\chapter{Chapter07 — PCPP Constructions}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from FABL.Chapter07.PCPPConstructions
\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter07.PCPPConstructions}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[All-zero Boolean string]
\lean{FABL.IsAllZeroString}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p029-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p179-b002
}
\label{FABL.IsAllZeroString}
\leanok
For a Boolean string $w$ of length $n$, the string is all zero if $w(i)=\mathrm{false}$
for every index $i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Constant Boolean string]
\lean{FABL.IsAllEqualString}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p034-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p179-b002
}
\label{FABL.IsAllEqualString}
\leanok
A Boolean string $w$ of length $n$ is constant if there is a bit
$b\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ such that $w(i)=b$ for every index $i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Boolean values and the field of two elements]
\lean{FABL.pcppBoolF₂Equiv}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.𝔽₂}
There is an equivalence between the two Boolean values and the elements of the field
with two elements.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Encoding false in the binary field]
\lean{FABL.pcppBoolF₂Equiv_false}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.pcppBoolF₂Equiv}
\difficulty{1}
The image of false under the standard equivalence between Boolean values and $\mathbb
F_2$ is zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Image of true]
\lean{FABL.pcppBoolF₂Equiv_true}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.pcppBoolF₂Equiv}
\difficulty{1}
Under the equivalence between Booleans and the field with two elements, `true` maps to
$1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Encoding Boolean negation in the binary field]
\lean{FABL.pcppBoolF₂Equiv_not}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.pcppBoolF₂Equiv}
\difficulty{4}
For every Boolean value $b$, the image of its negation under the standard equivalence
between Boolean values and $\mathbb F_2$ equals the image of $b$ plus $1$ in $\mathbb
F_2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Parity of a Boolean string]
\lean{FABL.boolStringParity}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p023-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p148-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p179-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p196-b002
}
\label{FABL.boolStringParity}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.pcppBoolF₂Equiv, FABL.𝔽₂}
For a Boolean string $w$ of length $n$, its parity is the sum in
$\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$ of the elements corresponding to its bits, with each bit mapped
to $0$ or $1$, respectively.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Odd-weight Boolean string]
\lean{FABL.IsOddWeightString}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p179-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p196-b002
}
\label{FABL.IsOddWeightString}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.boolStringParity}
A Boolean string $w$ of length $n$ has odd weight when its parity, computed in
$\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$, equals $1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Acceptance of a zero transcript]
\lean{FABL.allZeroTranscriptAccept}
\label{FABL.allZeroTranscriptAccept}
\leanok
Given a transcript with one position whose value is either absent or Boolean, the
acceptance value is true exactly when that position contains false.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Uniform one-query zero-string tester]
\lean{FABL.allZeroStringTester}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p179-b002}
\label{FABL.allZeroStringTester}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.NonadaptiveStringTester, FABL.allZeroTranscriptAccept, FABL.uniformPMF}
For a positive integer $n$, define a randomized nonadaptive tester for Boolean strings
of length $n$ by choosing an index uniformly from the $n$ positions, querying that
position, and applying the all-zero transcript acceptance predicate to the answer.
\end{definition}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p019-b003}
Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $w$ be a Boolean string of length $n$. The tester
that samples one coordinate uniformly and accepts exactly when the observed value is
false accepts $w$ with probability equal to the fraction of its entries that are false.
\end{theorem}

Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $w\colon\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ be a Boolean string.
The rejection probability of the tester that samples a coordinate uniformly and rejects
exactly when its value is $1$ equals the fraction of coordinates $i$ for which $w(i)=1$.
\end{theorem}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p181-b004}
For every positive integer $n$, the tester that samples one coordinate uniformly and
accepts exactly when its value is false is a local tester for the property of being the
all-false string, with rate $1$. It accepts the all-false string with probability $1$,
and for every $\varepsilon\in[0,1]$ and every string whose normalized Hamming distance
from the all-false string exceeds $\varepsilon$, its rejection probability is strictly
greater than $\varepsilon$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Acceptance of an equal-value transcript]
\lean{FABL.allEqualTranscriptAccept}
\label{FABL.allEqualTranscriptAccept}
\leanok
Given a transcript with two positions whose values are optional Booleans, the acceptance
value is true exactly when both positions contain Boolean values and those values are
equal.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Randomized two-query constant-string tester]
\lean{FABL.allEqualStringTester}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p179-b002}
\label{FABL.allEqualStringTester}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.NonadaptiveStringTester, FABL.allEqualTranscriptAccept, FABL.uniformPMF}
For $n>0$, define a randomized nonadaptive tester for Boolean strings of length $n$ by
choosing an ordered pair of indices independently and uniformly from the $n$ positions,
querying the bits at those indices, and applying the all-equal transcript acceptance
predicate to the resulting transcript.
\end{definition}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p181-b004}
Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $w$ be a Boolean string of length $n$. The
rejection probability of the tester that samples two coordinates independently and
uniformly and accepts exactly when their values agree equals the average, over all
ordered pairs of coordinates $(i,j)$, of $1$ when $w(i)\ne w(j)$ and $0$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p019-b003}
Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $w$ be a Boolean string of length $n$. The
rejection probability of the tester that samples two coordinates independently and
uniformly and accepts exactly when their values agree is twice the product of the
fraction of false entries and the fraction of true entries in $w$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Complementary Boolean probabilities]
\lean{FABL.uniformProbability_bool_false_add_true}
\label{FABL.uniformProbability_bool_false_add_true}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.uniformProbability}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a positive integer and let
$w:\operatorname{Fin}(n)\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ be a Boolean-valued
function. The uniform probabilities that $w(i)$ is false and that $w(i)$ is true sum to
$1$.
\end{theorem}

For every positive integer $n$, the tester that samples two coordinates independently
and uniformly and accepts exactly when their values agree is a local tester for the
property of being a constant Boolean string, with rate $1$. Specifically, it accepts
every constant string with probability $1$, and for every $\varepsilon\in[0,1]$ and
every string whose normalized Hamming distance from every constant string exceeds
$\varepsilon$, its rejection probability is strictly greater than $\varepsilon$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Certain acceptance and distribution support]
\lean{FABL.acceptanceProbability_eq_one_iff_accepts_on_support}
\label{FABL.acceptanceProbability_eq_one_iff_accepts_on_support}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.acceptanceProbability, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.accepts, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.transcript, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_const_one}
\difficulty{5}
Let $T$ be a nonadaptive function tester with seed distribution $
u$, and let $f$ map its domain to its alphabet. The acceptance probability of $T$ on $f$
is $1$ if and only if $T$ accepts $f$ for every seed in the support of $
u$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Coordinates queried by a tester]
\lean{FABL.queriedCoordinates}
\label{FABL.queriedCoordinates}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.NonadaptiveStringTester}
Let $T$ be a nonadaptive tester for Boolean strings of length $n$, and fix a seed for
$T$. The set of queried coordinates consists of those positions in the string that are
queried at some transcript position under that seed.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Bound on queried coordinates]
\lean{FABL.queriedCoordinates_card_le}
\label{FABL.queriedCoordinates_card_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.NonadaptiveStringTester, FABL.queriedCoordinates}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n,r$ be natural numbers, and let $T$ be a nonadaptive tester for Boolean strings of
length $n$ that makes $r$ query slots. For every seed of $T$, the number of distinct
string coordinates queried is at most $r$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[An unqueried coordinate]
\lean{FABL.exists_unqueried_coordinate}
\label{FABL.exists_unqueried_coordinate}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.NonadaptiveStringTester, FABL.queriedCoordinates, FABL.queriedCoordinates_card_le}
\difficulty{4}
Let a nonadaptive tester of Boolean strings of length $n$ make $r$ queries, and fix a
seed for its randomness. If $r<n$, then some coordinate is not queried at any of the
tester's $r$ transcript positions.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[String with one true coordinate]
\lean{FABL.singletonTrueString}
\label{FABL.singletonTrueString}
\leanok
For a position $i$ among the $n$ coordinates, define the Boolean string that is true at
$i$ and false at every other coordinate.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Odd weight of a singleton string]
\lean{FABL.singletonTrueString_isOddWeight}
\label{FABL.singletonTrueString_isOddWeight}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.IsOddWeightString, FABL.boolStringParity, FABL.pcppBoolF₂Equiv, FABL.singletonTrueString}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $i$ be a coordinate in $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. The
Boolean string that is true at $i$ and false at every other coordinate has odd Hamming
weight.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Transcript invariance under an unqueried coordinate]
\lean{FABL.singletonTrueString_transcript_eq}
\label{FABL.singletonTrueString_transcript_eq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.transcript, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.transcript_apply, FABL.NonadaptiveStringTester, FABL.singletonTrueString}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n,r$ be nonnegative integers, let $T$ be a nonadaptive tester of Boolean strings of
length $n$ using $r$ query positions, let $s$ be a seed of $T$, and let $i
e j$ be an arbitrary coordinate in $\{0,\dots,n-1\}$. If none of the query positions
for seed $s$ addresses coordinate $i$, then the transcript obtained by querying the
string that is true only at $i$ equals the transcript obtained by querying the
constantly false string.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Query lower bound for odd parity testing]
\lean{FABL.oddWeightString_no_localTester_of_queries_lt}
\label{FABL.oddWeightString_no_localTester_of_queries_lt}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.IsFar, FABL.IsLocalStringTester, FABL.IsOddWeightString, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.acceptanceProbability, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.accepts, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.rejectionProbability, FABL.NonadaptiveStringTester, FABL.acceptanceProbability_eq_one_iff_accepts_on_support, FABL.boolStringParity, FABL.exists_unqueried_coordinate, FABL.relativeHammingDist, FABL.singletonTrueString, FABL.singletonTrueString_isOddWeight, FABL.singletonTrueString_transcript_eq}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a positive natural number, and let a nonadaptive randomized tester query
Boolean strings of length $n$ at $r<n$ positions. For every real rate, this tester
cannot have perfect acceptance on all odd-parity strings and rejection probability
strictly greater than the rate times $\varepsilon$ on every string whose relative
Hamming distance from every odd-parity string exceeds $\varepsilon$, for all
$0\le\varepsilon\le1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Toggle a string coordinate]
\lean{FABL.toggleStringAt}
\label{FABL.toggleStringAt}
\leanok
Given a Boolean string $w$ of length $n$ and a coordinate $i$, the string obtained by
toggling at $i$ agrees with $w$ at every other coordinate and has the opposite Boolean
value at $i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Parity under a coordinate toggle]
\lean{FABL.boolStringParity_toggleStringAt}
\label{FABL.boolStringParity_toggleStringAt}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.boolStringParity, FABL.pcppBoolF₂Equiv, FABL.pcppBoolF₂Equiv_not, FABL.toggleStringAt}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $w\colon\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ be a Boolean string,
and choose a coordinate $i$. Toggling the bit of $w$ at $i$ changes its parity in
$\mathbb{F}_2$ by $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Toggling makes parity odd]
\lean{FABL.toggleStringAt_isOddWeight_of_not}
\label{FABL.toggleStringAt_isOddWeight_of_not}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.IsOddWeightString, FABL.boolStringParity, FABL.boolStringParity_toggleStringAt, FABL.f₂_eq_zero_or_one, FABL.toggleStringAt}
\difficulty{4}
Let $w$ be a length-$n$ Boolean string and let $i$ be one of its coordinates. If $w$ has
even Hamming weight, then the string obtained by toggling its bit at coordinate $i$ has
odd Hamming weight.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Distance After Toggling One Coordinate]
\lean{FABL.relativeHammingDist_toggleStringAt}
\label{FABL.relativeHammingDist_toggleStringAt}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.relativeHammingDist, FABL.toggleStringAt, FABL.uniformProbability, FABL.uniformProbability_ne_eq_relativeHammingDist}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a positive natural number, let
$w:\{1,\ldots,n\}\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ be a Boolean string, and let $i$
be one of its coordinates. The relative Hamming distance between $w$ and the string
obtained by toggling its $i$th coordinate is $1/n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Seed for the odd-weight partial-sum check]
\lean{FABL.OddWeightPartialSumCheckSeed}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p180-b003}
\label{FABL.OddWeightPartialSumCheckSeed}
\leanok
For a natural number $m$, a seed for the odd-weight partial-sum check is either a
Boolean bit or an index in $\{0,\ldots,m-1\}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Boolean prefix parity]
\lean{FABL.boolPrefixParity}
\label{FABL.boolPrefixParity}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.pcppBoolF₂Equiv, FABL.𝔽₂}
For a Boolean word $w$ of length $m+2$ and a natural number $k$, define its prefix
parity to be the sum in $mathbb{F}_2$ of the values corresponding to $w_i$ for $i<k$
and $i<m+2$; indices outside the word contribute zero.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Successive prefix parity]
\lean{FABL.boolPrefixParity_succ}
\label{FABL.boolPrefixParity_succ}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.boolPrefixParity, FABL.pcppBoolF₂Equiv}
\difficulty{3}
Let $m$ and $k$ be natural numbers, and let $w$ be a Boolean string of length $m+2$. If
$k<m+2$, then the parity of the first $k+1$ entries of $w$ is the parity of the first
$k$ entries plus, in $\mathbb{F}_2$, the encoding of the entry at position $k$.
\end{theorem}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p181-b004}
Let $m$ be a natural number and let $w$ be a Boolean string of length $m+2$. The sum in
$\mathbb{F}_2$ of the encoded values of all entries of $w$ equals the parity of its
prefix of length $m+2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Odd-weight partial-sum proof string]
\lean{FABL.oddWeightPartialSumProof}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p180-b003}
\label{FABL.oddWeightPartialSumProof}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.boolPrefixParity, FABL.pcppBoolF₂Equiv}
Given a Boolean string $w$ of length $m+2$, define a Boolean string of length $m+1$
whose entry at index $j$ is the bit corresponding to the parity of the prefix of $w$ of
length $j+2$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Linear triple transcript acceptance]
\lean{FABL.linearTripleTranscriptAccept}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p180-b003}
\label{FABL.linearTripleTranscriptAccept}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.pcppBoolF₂Equiv}
For a triple of possibly missing Boolean values, accept exactly when all three values
are present and, after identifying Booleans with elements of $\mathbb{F}_2$, the
third equals the sum of the first two.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Odd weight partial sum transcript acceptance]
\lean{FABL.oddWeightPartialSumTranscriptAccept}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p180-b003}
\label{FABL.oddWeightPartialSumTranscriptAccept}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.OddWeightPartialSumCheckSeed, FABL.linearTripleTranscriptAccept, FABL.pcppBoolF₂Equiv}
Let the seed be either a Boolean or an index in $\{0,\ldots,m-1\}$, and let a
transcript assign an optional Boolean to each of three positions. If the seed is false,
or is an index, accept exactly when all three answers are present and the third equals
the sum of the first two in $\mathbb{F}_2$. If the seed is true, accept exactly
when the first answer is present and equals $1$ in $\mathbb{F}_2$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Odd weight partial sum check]
\lean{FABL.OddWeightPartialSumCheckHolds}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p180-b003}
\label{FABL.OddWeightPartialSumCheckHolds}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.OddWeightPartialSumCheckSeed, FABL.pcppBoolF₂Equiv}
Let $m$ be a natural number, let the seed be either a Boolean or an index $k<m$, let $w$
assign Booleans to the $m+2$ input positions, and let $p$ assign Booleans to the $m+1$
proof positions. If the seed is false, then $p_0=w_0+w_1$ in $\mathbb{F}_2$. If
the seed is true, then the last proof bit is $1$ in $\mathbb{F}_2$. If the seed
is $k$, then $p_{k+1}=p_k+w_{k+2}$ in $\mathbb{F}_2$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Odd weight partial sum verifier]
\lean{FABL.oddWeightPartialSumPCPPSystem}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p179-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p180-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p180-b003
}
\label{FABL.oddWeightPartialSumPCPPSystem}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.OddWeightPartialSumCheckSeed, FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.oddWeightPartialSumTranscriptAccept, FABL.uniformPMF}
For each natural number $m$, define a verifier with $m+2$ Boolean input positions, $m+1$
Boolean proof positions, and three query positions. It samples uniformly from the seed
set consisting of two Boolean seeds and one seed for each index $k<m$. On the false seed
it queries input positions $0$ and $1$ and proof position $0$; on the true seed it
queries the last proof position and leaves the other two query positions unanswered; on
seed $k$ it queries proof position $k$, input position $k+2$, and proof position $k+1$.
It applies the corresponding transcript acceptance rule.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Verifier Acceptance and Check Validity]
\lean{FABL.oddWeightPartialSumPCPPSystem_accepts_iff}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p180-b003}

For every $m\in\mathbb{N}$, seed
$s\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}\sqcup\mathrm{Fin}(m)$, Boolean input word $w$ of
length $m+2$, and Boolean proof word $q$ of length $m+1$, the verifier of the odd-weight
partial-sum PCPP system accepts the combined input and proof on seed $s$ if and only if
the partial sum check specified by $s$ holds for $w$ and $q$.
\end{theorem}

For every $m\in\mathbb{N}$, Boolean input word $w$ of length $m+2$, and Boolean proof
word $q$ of length $m+1$, the rejection probability of the odd-weight partial-sum
verifier equals the uniform probability, over seeds in
$\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}\sqcup\mathrm{Fin}(m)$, that the corresponding
partial-sum check fails.
\end{theorem}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p180-b001}
Let $m\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $w$ be a Boolean word of length $m+2$ with odd weight.
Define the proof word $q$ of length $m+1$ by taking its $j$th bit to encode, in
$\mathbb{F}_2$, the parity of the first $j+2$ bits of $w$. Then every seed
$s\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}\sqcup\mathrm{Fin}(m)$ specifies a partial-sum
check that holds for $w$ and $q$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Odd parity from partial-sum checks]

Let $w\colon\{0,\ldots,m+1\}\to\{0,1\}$ and $p\colon\{0,\ldots,m\}\to\{0,1\}$. Suppose
the following checks hold: $p_0=w_0+w_1$ in $\mathbb F_2$; $p_m=1$ in $\mathbb F_2$;
and, for each $k<m$, $p_{k+1}=p_k+w_{k+2}$ in $\mathbb F_2$. Then the number of entries
of $w$ equal to $1$ is odd.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Failure probability for partial-sum checks]
\lean{FABL.one_div_length_le_failedCheckProbability}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p180-b003}
\label{FABL.one_div_length_le_failedCheckProbability}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.OddWeightPartialSumCheckHolds, FABL.OddWeightPartialSumCheckSeed, FABL.uniformProbability}
\difficulty{4}
Let $m$ be a natural number, let $w$ be a Boolean string of length $m+2$, and let $p$ be
a Boolean string of length $m+1$. Consider the $m+2$ checks consisting of the initial
check that $p_0=w_0+w_1$ modulo $2$, the final check that $p_m=1$, and, for each $k	ext{
with }0\le k<m$, the transition check that $p_{k+1}=p_k+w_{k+2}$ modulo $2$. If a
specified check in this collection fails, then a uniformly chosen check from the
collection fails with probability at least $1/(m+2)$.
\end{theorem}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p174-b001}
For every $m\in\mathbb{N}$, the odd-weight partial-sum PCPP system on Boolean strings of
length $m+2$, with proof strings of length $m+1$ and three query positions, has rate
$1$. Every input word of odd weight has a proof that the verifier accepts with
probability $1$. Moreover, for every $\varepsilon\in[0,1]$, if an input word is at
relative Hamming distance greater than $\varepsilon$ from every odd-weight word of
length $m+2$, then for every proof its rejection probability is strictly greater than
$\varepsilon$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Boolean sign correspondence]
\lean{FABL.pcppBoolSignEquiv}
\label{FABL.pcppBoolSignEquiv}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.binarySignEquiv, FABL.pcppBoolF₂Equiv}
Define the correspondence from Boolean values to signs ${pm 1}$ as the composition of
the correspondence from Booleans to $mathbb{F}_2$ and the binary-sign correspondence;
this is an equivalence.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Sign image of false]
\lean{FABL.pcppBoolSignEquiv_false}
\label{FABL.pcppBoolSignEquiv_false}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.pcppBoolSignEquiv}
\difficulty{1}
Under the Boolean-to-sign equivalence, `false` maps to $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Sign image of true]
\lean{FABL.pcppBoolSignEquiv_true}
\label{FABL.pcppBoolSignEquiv_true}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.pcppBoolSignEquiv}
\difficulty{1}
Under the Boolean-to-sign equivalence, `true` maps to $-1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Boolean string indexing]
\lean{FABL.booleanStringIndexEquiv}
\label{FABL.booleanStringIndexEquiv}
\leanok
For each natural number $n$, choose an equivalence between Boolean strings of length $n$
and the integers from $0$ through $2^n-1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Sign cube indexing equivalence]
\lean{FABL.signCubeIndexEquiv}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p023-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p023-b002
}
\label{FABL.signCubeIndexEquiv}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.SignCube}
For each natural number $N$, there is an equivalence between the set of length-$N$ sign
vectors, with entries in $\{ -1,1\}$, and the set of integers from $0$ through
$2^N-1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Proof function on the sign cube]
\lean{FABL.pcppProofFunction}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p181-b004}
\label{FABL.pcppProofFunction}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.pcppBoolSignEquiv, FABL.signCubeIndexEquiv}
For each natural number $N$ and each Boolean-valued function on the integers from $0$
through $2^N-1$, define a function on length-$N$ sign vectors by indexing the Boolean
function with the corresponding integer and identifying its Boolean output with a sign.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Encoding a Boolean function as a proof]
\lean{FABL.encodeBooleanFunctionProof}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p181-b004}
\label{FABL.encodeBooleanFunctionProof}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.pcppBoolSignEquiv, FABL.signCubeIndexEquiv}
For each natural number $N$ and each function from length-$N$ sign vectors to signs,
define a Boolean-valued function on the integers from $0$ through $2^N-1$ by converting
each index to its corresponding sign vector, evaluating the given function there, and
converting the resulting sign to a Boolean.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Encoding a Boolean function as a proof]
\lean{FABL.pcppProofFunction_encodeBooleanFunctionProof}
\label{FABL.pcppProofFunction_encodeBooleanFunctionProof}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.encodeBooleanFunctionProof, FABL.pcppProofFunction}
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $N$ and every function $f:\{ -1,1\}^N\to\{ -1,1\}$, encode its
values as Booleans indexed by the $2^N$ points of the sign cube, then decode that
Boolean function on the sign cube. The resulting function is $f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Recovery of an indexed Boolean function]
\lean{FABL.encodeBooleanFunctionProof_pcppProofFunction}
\label{FABL.encodeBooleanFunctionProof_pcppProofFunction}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.encodeBooleanFunctionProof, FABL.pcppProofFunction}
\difficulty{3}
Let $N$ be a natural number, and let $q$ assign a Boolean value to each of the $2^N$
indices. Define a sign-valued function on the $N$-dimensional sign cube by reading $q$
at the index corresponding to each sign vector and converting its Boolean value to a
sign. If this function is converted back to an indexed Boolean function by evaluating it
at the sign vector corresponding to each index and converting the sign back to a Boolean
value, the result is exactly $q$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Coordinate truth table]
\lean{FABL.coordinateTruthTable}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p181-b004}
\label{FABL.coordinateTruthTable}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.SignCube, FABL.booleanStringIndexEquiv, FABL.pcppBoolSignEquiv}
For each natural number $n$ and coordinate $j<n$, define a length-$2^n$ sign vector
whose entry at index $i$ is $-1$ or $1$ according to the $j$th bit of the $n$-bit
Boolean string indexed by $i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Coordinate truth table evaluation]
\lean{FABL.coordinateTruthTable_apply_index}
\label{FABL.coordinateTruthTable_apply_index}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.booleanStringIndexEquiv, FABL.coordinateTruthTable, FABL.pcppBoolSignEquiv}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $w$ be a Boolean string of length $n$, and let $j$ be
one of its coordinates. Evaluating the $j$th coordinate truth table at the index
assigned to $w$ gives the sign corresponding to the bit $w_j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Truth table indices satisfying a property]
\lean{FABL.propertyIndexSet}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p181-b004}
\label{FABL.propertyIndexSet}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.booleanStringIndexEquiv}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $P$ be a property of Boolean strings of length $n$.
The property index set consists of those indices in $	ext{Fin}(2^n)$ whose corresponding
Boolean string satisfies $P$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Membership in a property index set]
\lean{FABL.mem_propertyIndexSet}
\label{FABL.mem_propertyIndexSet}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.booleanStringIndexEquiv, FABL.propertyIndexSet}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $P$ be a property of Boolean strings of length $n$, and
let $w$ be such a string. The index assigned to $w$ belongs to the set of indices for
strings satisfying $P$ if and only if $P(w)$ holds.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Boolean truth table lift of a tester]
\lean{FABL.boolTruthTableLiftTester}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p181-b004}
\label{FABL.boolTruthTableLiftTester}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester, FABL.Sign, FABL.SignCube, FABL.pcppBoolSignEquiv, FABL.signCubeIndexEquiv}
Let $T$ be a randomized nonadaptive tester that makes $r$ queries to sign-valued
functions on the sign cube of dimension $N$, and let $n$ be a natural number. The lifted
tester uses the same seed distribution and acceptance rule, converts each queried
sign-cube point to its truth-table index, and queries that index in the truth-table
portion of the disjoint address space; it converts Boolean answers back to signs before
applying $T$'s acceptance rule.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Transcript of the lifted tester]
\lean{FABL.boolTruthTableLiftTester_visibleTranscript}
\label{FABL.boolTruthTableLiftTester_visibleTranscript}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.transcript, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.transcript_apply, FABL.Sign, FABL.SignCube, FABL.boolTruthTableLiftTester, FABL.inputProofWord, FABL.pcppBoolSignEquiv, FABL.pcppProofFunction}
\difficulty{4}
Let $T$ be a finite-seed randomized nonadaptive tester making $r$ queries to functions
from $\{\pm1\}^N$ to $\{\pm1\}$. For any nonnegative integer $n$, Boolean string
$w\in\{0,1\}^n$, Boolean proof table $p\colon\{0,1,\ldots,2^N-1\}\to\{0,1\}$, and seed
of $T$, converting each answer in the lifted tester's transcript on the concatenated
input $(w,p)$ from a Boolean value to a sign gives exactly the transcript of $T$ on the
sign-valued function on the sign cube encoded by $p$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Acceptance probability of the lifted tester]
\lean{FABL.boolTruthTableLiftTester_acceptanceProbability}
\label{FABL.boolTruthTableLiftTester_acceptanceProbability}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.acceptanceProbability, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.transcript, FABL.Sign, FABL.SignCube, FABL.boolTruthTableLiftTester, FABL.boolTruthTableLiftTester_visibleTranscript, FABL.inputProofWord, FABL.pcppBoolSignEquiv, FABL.pcppProofFunction, FABL.pmfExpectation}
\difficulty{4}
Let $T$ be a finite-seed randomized nonadaptive tester that makes $r$ queries to
functions from the sign cube $\{\pm1\}^N$ to $\{\pm1\}$. For any nonnegative integer
$n$, Boolean string $w\in\{0,1\}^n$, and proof table
$p\colon\{0,1,\ldots,2^N-1\}\to\{0,1\}$, the tester obtained by redirecting $T$'s
queries to the proof-table portion of the input and converting Boolean answers to signs
has the same acceptance probability on the concatenated input $(w,p)$ as $T$ has on the
sign-valued function on the sign cube encoded by $p$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Coordinate true-index set]
\lean{FABL.coordinateTrueIndexSet}
\label{FABL.coordinateTrueIndexSet}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.booleanStringIndexEquiv}
For a natural number $n$ and a coordinate $j$ among the $n$ positions, let the
associated set consist of all indices in ${0,\ldots,2^n-1}$ whose corresponding Boolean
string has value true at coordinate $j$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Membership in the true-coordinate index set]
\lean{FABL.mem_coordinateTrueIndexSet}
\label{FABL.mem_coordinateTrueIndexSet}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.booleanStringIndexEquiv, FABL.coordinateTrueIndexSet}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $j$ be a coordinate in $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let $i$
index a Boolean string of length $n$. Then $i$ belongs to the set of indices whose
string has value true at coordinate $j$ if and only if the string indexed by $i$ has
value true at coordinate $j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Coordinate truth table representation]
\lean{FABL.subsetIndicatorSign_coordinateTrueIndexSet}
\label{FABL.subsetIndicatorSign_coordinateTrueIndexSet}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.booleanStringIndexEquiv, FABL.coordinateTrueIndexSet, FABL.coordinateTruthTable, FABL.subsetIndicatorSign}
\difficulty{4}
For every natural number $n$ and coordinate $j\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, the sign vector that
is $-1$ precisely at indices encoding Boolean strings whose $j$th bit is true, and $1$
elsewhere, equals the truth table of the $j$th coordinate, with true encoded by $-1$ and
false by $1$.
\end{theorem}

\lean{FABL.coordinateLocalCorrection_correctProbability_ge}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p182-b001}

\proofstep
  {FABL.coordinateLocalCorrection_correctProbability_ge}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p033-b003,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p174-b003}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f$ map the sign cube of dimension $2^n$ to the
signs $\{-1,1\}$, and choose coordinates $j\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ and
$i\in\{0,\ldots,2^n-1\}$. Let $\varepsilon\in[0,1]$, and suppose the fraction of inputs
on which $f$ differs from the dictator reading coordinate $i$ is at most
$0.2\varepsilon$. For a uniformly random $y$ in the binary cube of dimension $2^n$,
convert $f$ to a sign-valued function $g$ on that binary cube using the coordinatewise
identification of bits with signs, and let $a$ be the sign string whose entry at a
binary string $z$ is the sign corresponding to bit $j$ of $z$. Then the probability that
$g(y)g(y+a)$ equals the sign corresponding to bit $j$ of the binary string indexed by
$i$ is at least $1-0.4\varepsilon$ and at least $1/2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Coordinate correction probability]
\lean{FABL.coordinateCorrectionProbability}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p182-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p182-b002
}
\label{FABL.coordinateCorrectionProbability}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.binaryCubeSignEquiv, FABL.coordinateTruthTable, FABL.localCorrection, FABL.pcppBoolSignEquiv, FABL.uniformProbability}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a sign-valued Boolean function on strings of
length $2^n$, let $j$ be a coordinate in $	ext{Fin}(n)$, and let $b$ be a Boolean bit.
The coordinate correction probability is the uniform probability over Boolean strings
$y$ of length $2^n$ that the local correction of the sign version of $f$, at the truth
table encoding the $j$th coordinate, evaluated at $y$, equals the sign corresponding to
$b$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Coordinate consistency acceptance rule]
\lean{FABL.coordinateConsistencyTranscriptAccept}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p182-b002}
\label{FABL.coordinateConsistencyTranscriptAccept}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.pcppBoolSignEquiv}
Given three optional Boolean answers, reject unless all three are present. If they are
present, accept exactly when the product of the signs corresponding to the second and
third answers equals the sign corresponding to the first answer.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Coordinate consistency tester]
\lean{FABL.coordinateConsistencyFunctionTester}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p182-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p182-b002
}
\label{FABL.coordinateConsistencyFunctionTester}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester, FABL.binaryCubeSignEquiv, FABL.coordinateConsistencyTranscriptAccept, FABL.coordinateTruthTable, FABL.signCubeIndexEquiv, FABL.uniformPMF}
Let $n$ be a positive natural number. Choose uniformly a coordinate $j$ and a Boolean
string $y$ of length $2^n$. The tester makes three queries: the input bit at $j$, and
the proof-table entries indexed by the sign encodings of $y$ and $x+y$, where $x$ is the
sign encoding of the truth table of the $j$th coordinate function. It accepts exactly
when the three answers satisfy the coordinate consistency rule: the product of the signs
from the two proof answers equals the sign from the input answer.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Acceptance probability of the coordinate consistency tester]
\lean{FABL.coordinateConsistencyFunctionTester_acceptanceProbability}
\label{FABL.coordinateConsistencyFunctionTester_acceptanceProbability}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.acceptanceProbability, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.transcript_apply, FABL.coordinateConsistencyFunctionTester, FABL.coordinateConsistencyTranscriptAccept, FABL.coordinateCorrectionProbability, FABL.inputProofWord, FABL.pcppProofFunction, FABL.pmfExpectation_uniformPMF_eq_expect, FABL.uniformPMF, FABL.uniformProbability}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n\ge1$, let $w:\{1,\ldots,n\}\to\{0,1\}$, and let a proof table assign a bit to
each of the $2^{2^n}$ sign vectors of length $2^n$. The nonadaptive tester chooses a
coordinate uniformly from $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and a vector $y$ uniformly from $\mathbb
F_2^{2^n}$, queries the corresponding input bit and two proof bits associated with $y$
and its translate by the truth table of that coordinate, and accepts exactly when the
product of the two proof signs equals the input sign. Its acceptance probability on this
input and proof equals the uniform average over coordinates $j$ of the probability that
the local correction of the proof agrees with $w(j)$, where the correction at $y$ is the
product of the proof signs at $y$ and at its translate by the coordinate truth table.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Local correction of a dictator]
\lean{FABL.coordinateLocalCorrection_dictator}
\label{FABL.coordinateLocalCorrection_dictator}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.binaryCubeSignEquiv, FABL.booleanStringIndexEquiv, FABL.coordinateTruthTable, FABL.coordinateTruthTable_apply_index, FABL.dictator, FABL.localCorrection, FABL.pcppBoolSignEquiv, FABL.signEncode, FABL.signEncode_add}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $w:\{0,1\}^n$ be a Boolean string, let $j$ be a
coordinate, and let $y$ be an $\mathbb F_2$-valued vector indexed by the Boolean
strings of length $n$. Encode each Boolean string as a sign vector coordinatewise, and
use the truth table of the $j$th bit as the input to the local correction of the
dictator that reads the coordinate indexed by $w$. The resulting sign is the encoding of
the bit $w_j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Property truth table tester]
\lean{FABL.propertyTruthTableFunctionTester}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p181-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p182-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p182-b002
}
\label{FABL.propertyTruthTableFunctionTester}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester, FABL.boolTruthTableLiftTester, FABL.dictatorSubclassFunctionTester, FABL.propertyIndexSet}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $P$ be a property of Boolean strings of length $n$.
The tester is the Boolean truth-table lift, with $n$ input coordinates, of the
three-query dictator-subclass tester indexed by the truth-table indices whose
corresponding strings satisfy $P$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[PCPP system for an arbitrary property]
\lean{FABL.arbitraryPropertyPCPPSystem}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p179-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p180-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p181-b004
}
\label{FABL.arbitraryPropertyPCPPSystem}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.coordinateConsistencyFunctionTester, FABL.propertyTruthTableFunctionTester, FABL.uniformMixtureFunctionTester}
Let $n$ be a positive natural number and let $P$ be a property of Boolean strings of
length $n$. The system has proof length $2^{2^n}$ and uses three queries. Its verifier
chooses with equal probability between the property truth-table tester and the
coordinate consistency tester.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Acceptance probability of the mixed verifier]
\lean{FABL.arbitraryPropertyPCPPSystem_acceptanceProbability}
\label{FABL.arbitraryPropertyPCPPSystem_acceptanceProbability}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.acceptanceProbability, FABL.PCPPSystem.acceptanceProbability, FABL.arbitraryPropertyPCPPSystem, FABL.coordinateConsistencyFunctionTester, FABL.inputProofWord, FABL.propertyTruthTableFunctionTester, FABL.uniformMixtureFunctionTester_acceptanceProbability}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a positive natural number, let $P$ be any property of Boolean strings of
length $n$, let $w$ be such a string, and let $q$ be a Boolean proof string of length
$2^{2^n}$. The acceptance probability of the verifier formed by choosing uniformly
between the property-testing verifier and the coordinate-consistency verifier, on input
$w$ and proof $q$, is the arithmetic mean of the acceptance probabilities of those two
verifiers on the concatenated input and proof.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Completeness for arbitrary properties]
\lean{FABL.arbitraryPropertyPCPPSystem_complete}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p180-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p181-b004
}
\label{FABL.arbitraryPropertyPCPPSystem_complete}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.NonadaptiveFunctionTester.acceptanceProbability, FABL.PCPPSystem.acceptanceProbability, FABL.arbitraryPropertyPCPPSystem, FABL.arbitraryPropertyPCPPSystem_acceptanceProbability, FABL.binaryCubeSignEquiv, FABL.boolTruthTableLiftTester_acceptanceProbability, FABL.booleanStringIndexEquiv, FABL.coordinateConsistencyFunctionTester, FABL.coordinateConsistencyFunctionTester_acceptanceProbability, FABL.coordinateCorrectionProbability, FABL.coordinateLocalCorrection_dictator, FABL.coordinateTruthTable, FABL.dictator, FABL.dictatorSubclass_isLocalTester, FABL.encodeBooleanFunctionProof, FABL.inputProofWord, FABL.localCorrection, FABL.mem_propertyIndexSet, FABL.pcppBoolSignEquiv, FABL.pcppProofFunction_encodeBooleanFunctionProof, FABL.propertyIndexSet, FABL.propertyTruthTableFunctionTester, FABL.uniformProbability}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $P$ be a property of Boolean strings of length $n$,
and let $w$ be such a string with $P(w)$. The PCPP system for $P$, on input $w$ and the
proof encoding the dictator function that evaluates each sign vector at the coordinate
indexed by $w$, accepts with probability $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Upper bound for coordinate correction probability]
\lean{FABL.coordinateCorrectionProbability_le_one}
\label{FABL.coordinateCorrectionProbability_le_one}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.binaryCubeSignEquiv, FABL.coordinateCorrectionProbability, FABL.coordinateTruthTable, FABL.localCorrection, FABL.pcppBoolSignEquiv, FABL.uniformProbability}
\difficulty{3}
For every $n\in\mathbb N$, every Boolean function $f:\{−1,1\}^{2^n}\to\{−1,1\}$, every
coordinate $j\in\mathrm{Fin}(n)$, and every bit $b\in\{0,1\}$, the probability that the
local correction of $f$ agrees with the sign encoding of $b$, under a uniformly random
input in $\mathbb F_2^{2^n}$, is at most $1$.
\end{theorem}

  {FABL.coordinateCorrectionProbability}
  {context}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p177-b007,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p182-b001}
\proofstep
  {FABL.coordinateCorrectionProbability_le_one}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p177-b007,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p182-b001}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a sign-valued Boolean function on the sign cube
of dimension $2^n$, and let $w,w_0$ be Boolean strings of length $n$. For a coordinate
$j$, form its truth-table sign vector on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube, and consider
the local correction of the function obtained from $f$ by the coordinatewise
binary-to-sign encoding, in the direction corresponding to that vector. If this
correction equals the sign encoded by $w_0(j)$ with probability at least $1/2$ for a
uniformly random point of the cube, then the probability that it fails to equal the sign
encoded by $w(j)$ is at least $1/2$ when $w(j)\ne w_0(j)$, and is at least zero when
they agree.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[PCPP description for an arbitrary property]
\lean{FABL.arbitraryPropertyPCPPDescription}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p181-b004}
\label{FABL.arbitraryPropertyPCPPDescription}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.PCPPDescription, FABL.arbitraryPropertyPCPPSystem, FABL.arbitraryPropertyPCPPSystem_isPCPP}
Let $n$ be a positive natural number and let $P$ be a property of Boolean strings of
length $n$. There is a description of a probabilistically checkable proof system with
proof length $2^{2^n}$, query count $3$, and rejection rate $1/1000$, whose system is
the verifier given by the equal-probability mixture of the property truth-table tester
and coordinate consistency tester, and which satisfies the PCPP conditions for $P$ at
that rejection rate.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Existence of a PCPP for every Boolean property]
\lean{FABL.exists_arbitraryPropertyPCPPSystem}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p181-b004}
\label{FABL.exists_arbitraryPropertyPCPPSystem}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.IsPCPP, FABL.PCPPSystem, FABL.arbitraryPropertyPCPPSystem, FABL.arbitraryPropertyPCPPSystem_isPCPP}
\difficulty{1}
For every natural number $n>0$ and every property $P$ of Boolean strings of length $n$,
there is a probabilistically checkable proof system with proof length $2^{2^n}$ and a
verifier making three nonadaptive queries, such that every string satisfying $P$ has a
proof accepted with probability $1$. Moreover, for every $\varepsilon\in[0,1]$, any
input whose relative Hamming distance from every string satisfying $P$ is greater than
$\varepsilon$ is rejected, for every proof, with probability greater than
$\varepsilon/1000$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Circuit semantic PCPP reduction]
\lean{FABL.exhaustiveCircuitSemanticPCPPReduction}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p182-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p182-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p183-b002
}
\label{FABL.exhaustiveCircuitSemanticPCPPReduction}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanCircuit.acceptedProperty, FABL.SemanticPCPPReduction, FABL.arbitraryPropertyPCPPDescription}
For every positive integer $n$, assign to each Boolean circuit on $n$ input bits a PCPP
description for the property consisting of inputs accepted by that circuit.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Resources of the exhaustive circuit reduction]
\lean{FABL.exhaustiveCircuitSemanticPCPPReduction_resources}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p183-b002,

}

\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanCircuit, FABL.arbitraryPropertyPCPPDescription, FABL.exhaustiveCircuitSemanticPCPPReduction}
\difficulty{1}
For every positive integer $n$ and every Boolean circuit $C$ on $n$ input bits, the
associated PCPP description has proof length $2^{2^n}$, query count $3$, and rejection
rate $1/1000$.
\end{theorem}
